title: Adivasi students detained in Mumbai after march from Nashik over hostel conditions
seoTitle: Mumbai: Adivasi students detained after march

tea.why: Adivasi students protested new government rules for hostels, alleging poor facilities, unsafe conditions, and student deaths.

tea.changed: Oct 6: Police detained students at the Congress office in Mumbai and transported them out of the city.

summary: Adivasi students marched from Nashik to Mumbai, arriving on October 4, to protest against new government rules for student hostels, poor facilities, and student deaths. They had planned a demonstration at Azad Maidan but were allegedly detained by police at the Maharashtra Congress office on October 5. The students were subsequently transported out of Mumbai on October 6. The Maharashtra Congress provided shelter to the students and condemned the police action, with leaders like Harshvardhan Sapkal and Varsha Gaikwad speaking out. Demands included improved hostel facilities, scholarships, an independent probe into student deaths, compensation for victims' families, and the resignation of Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike. Police denied arresting anyone from the Congress office, stating they were detaining protesters from various locations who planned to march to Lok Bhavan.
demands: Provide basic facilities in tribal ashram schools and hostels
Conduct an independent probe into student deaths at tribal schools
Provide ₹1 crore compensation to families of three girls who died of snakebite
Resignation of Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike
response: Police denied arresting anyone from the Congress office, stating they were detaining protesters from various locations who planned to march to Lok Bhavan. Students were later put on private buses and taken out of Mumbai.

updates.text: Adivasi students began a march from Nashik towards Mumbai to protest various grievances related to tribal development.
Students reached Mumbai late Sunday night and were provided shelter at the Maharashtra Congress headquarters in Dadar.
Police allegedly detained Adivasi students at the Maharashtra Congress office ahead of a planned protest at Azad Maidan.
Maharashtra Congress leaders demanded the immediate release of detained students and threatened to gherao the Chief Minister's residence.
Police denied arresting anyone from the Congress office, stating they were detaining protesters planning to march to Lok Bhavan from various locations.
Students were stopped from leaving the Congress office, put on private buses, and transported out of Mumbai.
